findings.claim: Snapshot delivery lacks the app-layer tenant/type equality guard and can emit protected snapshot records returned by the projection even if they are for another tenant or type.
findings.evidence: In `snapshot_frames`, the loop over `rows: Vec<EntityTypeDelivery>` only checks `self.authz.check(&object_view_tuple(request.tenant_id, subject, &delivery.mutation.key))` before pushing `SnapshotRow`; unlike live delivery in `entity_type_watch/stream.rs`, it never verifies `delivery.mutation.tenant_id == request.tenant_id` or `request.entity_type.matches(&delivery.mutation)`. This conflicts with acceptance A requiring other tenants/types receive no protected payload and constraint S4 requiring tenant isolation at Keto plus the app-layer tenant-equality guard.
findings.suggested_fix: In `snapshot_frames`, before object authorization, fail closed or skip rows whose `delivery.mutation.tenant_id != request.tenant_id` or whose mutation does not match `request.entity_type`; keep the app-layer guard independent of projection correctness.

findings.claim: New public enums are missing `#[non_exhaustive]`, contrary to the workspace Rust idiom constraint.
findings.evidence: Constraint I1 says `#[non_exhaustive]` on public enums; this file adds public enums `TypeWatchStart`, `ResnapshotReason`, and `EntityTypeWatchFrame` without the attribute.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to the new public enums or document why these public APIs are intentionally exhaustive.
